questions.text:
Consider the functions

I. [latex]e^{-x}[/latex]
II. [latex]x^2-\sin x[/latex]
III. [latex]\sqrt{x^3+1}[/latex]

Which of the above functions is/are increasing everywhere in [0,1] ?
questions.solution:
Check the derivative on [0, 1]:
- I: [latex](e^{-x})'=-e^{-x} \lt 0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decreasing.
- II: [latex]2x-\cos x[/latex] is [latex]-1[/latex] at x = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decreasing near 0.
- III: [latex]\frac{3x^2}{2\sqrt{x^3+1}}\ge0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] increasing on the whole interval.

Answer: III only

questions.text: For parameters a and b, both of which are [latex]\omega(1) , T(n)=T(n^{1/a})+1[/latex], and [latex]T(b)=1[/latex]. Then [latex]T(n)[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Each step takes the a-th root: [latex]n\rightarrow n^{1/a}\rightarrow n^{1/a^2}\rightarrow\cdots[/latex], until it reaches b.

[latex]n^{1/a^k}=b\Rightarrow\frac{\log_b n}{a^k}=1\Rightarrow k=\log_a\log_b n[/latex]

Each step adds 1, so [latex]T(n)=\Theta(\log_a\log_b n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(\log_a\log_b n)[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.

I. Daisy chaining is used to assign priorities in attending interrupts.
II. When a device raises a vectored interrupt, the CPU does polling to identify the source of interrupt.
III. In polling,the CPU periodically checks the status bits to know if any device needs its attention.
IV. During DMA, both the CPU and DMA controller can be bus masters at the same time.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: daisy chaining serially connects devices; the one nearest the CPU gets highest priority [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- II: a vectored interrupt supplies the ISR address itself, so no polling is needed [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- III: that is the definition of polling [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- IV: only one bus master at a time; the CPU gives up the bus during DMA [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: I and III only

questions.text:
Consider the following data path diagram.

Consider an instruction: [latex]R0\leftarrow R1+R2[/latex]. The following steps are used to execute it over the given data path. Assume that PC is incremented appropriately. The subscripts r and w indicate read and write operations, respectively.

[latex]1. \; R2_r,TEMP1_r,ALU_{add},TEMP2_w[/latex]
[latex]2. \; R1_r,TEMP1_w[/latex]
[latex]3. \; PC_r,MAR_w,MEM_r[/latex]
[latex]4. \; TEMP2_r,R0_w[/latex]
[latex]5. \; MDR_r,IR_w[/latex]

Which one of the following is the correct order of execution of the above steps?
questions.solution:
First fetch the instruction, then execute it:
- 3: PC [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] MAR, read memory (fetch)
- 5: MDR [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] IR (instruction now in IR)
- 2: R1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] TEMP1 (one ALU input is latched in TEMP1)
- 1: R2 on the bus + TEMP1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ALU add [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] TEMP2
- 4: TEMP2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R0

Answer: 3, 5, 2, 1, 4

questions.text: The preorder traversal of a binary search tree is 15,10,12,11,20,18,16,19. Which one of the following is the postorder traversal of the tree?
questions.solution:
Build the BST from the preorder (root first):
- Root 15; left subtree {10, 12, 11}: 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] right 12 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] left 11.
- Right subtree {20, 18, 16, 19}: 20 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] left 18 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] children 16 and 19.

Postorder (left, right, root): 11, 12, 10, 16, 19, 18, 20, 15

Answer: 11, 12, 10, 16, 19, 18, 20, 15
